title: URL shortener
seoTitle: URL Shortener with Analytics & Smart Routing | Linktery
seoDescription: Create short, trackable URLs, edit destinations, use branded domains, and understand clicks by device, location, source, and campaign.
lead: Create a compact URL for a destination, then update its settings without replacing the link you shared.

highlights.title: Editable destination
highlights.text: Keep the short address while changing the destination.

highlights.title: Campaign parameters
highlights.text: Set UTM source, medium, and campaign values in the editor.

highlights.title: Optional routing
highlights.text: Device rules are available on all plans; geo targeting and A/B splitting depend on your plan.

sections.heading: Create and share
paragraphs: Open Links, add an HTTP or HTTPS destination, and choose an available platform domain. Copy the generated short address into your post, message, or QR code.
bullets: Generated short URLs on every plan
Custom Smart Link slugs on Agency
Unique addresses across Links and profiles

sections.heading: Update your link
paragraphs: Edit the destination, active status, or schedule from Links. Destination changes keep the same public URL; changing its slug or domain changes the address you share.

Before replacing a campaign offer, open the published short URL and confirm the final page, including any campaign parameters. This also checks links already embedded in messages or printed materials.
bullets: Test the public address after updates

sections.heading: Choose the right format
paragraphs: Use a Smart Link for a redirect or a Public Profile for a page of choices. Advanced traffic breakdowns are a paid analytics feature, not part of every Free account report.
bullets: Custom domains open at the root

faqs.question: Can I change the destination later?
faqs.answer: Yes. Update it in Links while keeping the published short URL.

faqs.question: Can I choose my own short-link slug?
faqs.answer: Custom Smart Link slugs are included on Agency. Other plans use generated short addresses.

faqs.question: Is a Public Profile also a redirect?
faqs.answer: No. It displays a page where visitors choose between your cards.

title: Link management
seoTitle: Link Management Platform for Creators & Teams | Linktery
seoDescription: Manage short URLs, public profiles, branded domains, QR codes, routing rules, and click analytics from one Linktery workspace.
lead: Maintain published addresses, content, and destinations from the Links and Public Profiles editors.

highlights.title: Link controls
highlights.text: Edit destinations, UTM values, active status, and routing.

highlights.title: Profile editing
highlights.text: Update appearance, content blocks, and the order of your cards.

highlights.title: Domain attachments
highlights.text: See the custom domain attached to each resource alongside its platform address.

sections.heading: Use the right editor
paragraphs: Links manages redirects. Public Profiles manages multi-link pages. Each resource has its own editor and published address.

sections.heading: Maintain published content
paragraphs: Review destinations when an offer changes or a campaign ends. Keeping a Link's public address unchanged also keeps QR codes pointing to that address useful after a destination update.

Keep a record of where each address is published, such as social bios, newsletters, packaging, or advertisements. That makes it easier to assess which placements need attention before changing a domain or retiring a resource.

sections.heading: Account and plan scope
paragraphs: Resource counts and advanced settings depend on your plan. The current workspace is account-based: team seats, invitations, and role-based publishing permissions are not included.
bullets: Links and profiles have separate allowances

faqs.question: Can I manage Links and Public Profiles together?
faqs.answer: Yes. They share your account, with a dedicated editor for each resource type.

faqs.question: Do edits require a new address?
faqs.answer: Content and destination edits can keep the existing address. Renaming a slug or changing a domain changes the address itself.

faqs.question: Does Agency include team seats?
faqs.answer: No. The current product does not include shared workspace seats or role-based team permissions.

title: Branded links
seoTitle: Branded Short Links & Custom Link Domains | Linktery
seoDescription: Use a custom domain for recognizable short links and public profiles while managing destinations, routing, and analytics in Linktery.
lead: Choose your public address: a platform domain, a custom Smart Link slug, or a domain you own.

highlights.title: Platform domains
highlights.text: Choose from the domains offered in your resource editor.

highlights.title: Custom short-link slugs
highlights.text: Agency lets you replace a generated Smart Link slug with a readable name.

highlights.title: Your own host
highlights.text: Pro and Agency can connect an owned domain at its root address.

sections.heading: Two address formats
paragraphs: Platform addresses use a domain plus a slug, such as linktery.com/launch. Owned domains work differently: go.yourbrand.com opens one attached Link or Public Profile without a /slug.
bullets: Custom Smart Link slugs require Agency

sections.heading: Address and destination
paragraphs: The address is what you share; Link settings determine the redirect destination. A Public Profile renders a page instead. Updating the destination or profile content can keep your existing address.

sections.heading: Publish a verified domain
paragraphs: Complete the Custom Domains setup and wait for DNS and HTTPS readiness. Use a dedicated subdomain if your main domain already serves a website.
Check the exact hostname you intend to share, not only the account setup screen. Keep your current website and email records intact while following the DNS instructions for the new hostname.

faqs.question: Can I use go.yourbrand.com/launch?
faqs.answer: Custom domains attach to one resource at the root, such as go.yourbrand.com, without a /slug. Platform domains use the domain-and-slug format.

faqs.question: Which plan includes custom Smart Link slugs?
faqs.answer: Agency. Owned domains are available on Creator Pro and Agency.

faqs.question: Can a custom domain open a Public Profile?
faqs.answer: Yes. Attach the verified domain to the profile; it will open at the domain's root.

title: Link analytics
seoTitle: Link Analytics & URL Click Tracking | Linktery
seoDescription: Track short-link clicks and public-profile engagement by time, destination, country, device, browser, referrer, and campaign.
lead: Read click trends and traffic breakdowns by date, country, device, source, and campaign.

highlights.title: Traffic over time
highlights.text: Compare activity across reporting periods.

highlights.title: Traffic context
highlights.text: Inspect supported country, device, browser, referrer, and UTM dimensions.

highlights.title: Per-link scope
highlights.text: Review a particular Link instead of only account-wide totals.

sections.heading: Read your report
paragraphs: Choose a date range and Link, then move from overall activity to individual breakdowns. Full analytics is included on Creator Pro and Agency; basic dashboard totals are not the same as advanced reports.

sections.heading: Keep attribution consistent
paragraphs: Use consistent UTM source, medium, and campaign names. Some apps omit referrer information, so a missing referrer does not prove that a URL was typed directly.

Agree on one naming convention before distributing campaign URLs. Using different spellings for the same campaign makes reports harder to compare, even when every link reaches the correct destination.

sections.heading: Interpret the metrics
paragraphs: Link clicks do not prove sales or signups; measure those at the destination. Events are processed asynchronously, so fresh activity may take a short time to appear. Location and device dimensions are approximate.
bullets: Do not treat network signals as identity

faqs.question: Why is a new click not visible immediately?
faqs.answer: Analytics is processed asynchronously. Allow a short time for new activity to appear and the report to refresh.

faqs.question: Does a click prove a conversion?
faqs.answer: No. Sales and signups must be measured at the destination or through a suitable downstream integration.

faqs.question: Where are profile card clicks?
faqs.answer: Public Profile analytics separates profile views from clicks on individual cards.

title: Custom domains
seoTitle: Custom Domains for Short Links & Bio Pages | Linktery
seoDescription: Connect an owned domain at its root to one Link or Public Profile. Pro includes 2 custom domains, Agency 10, with DNS verification and HTTPS.
lead: Attach a domain you own to one Smart Link or Public Profile. Visitors open the domain directly, with no /slug.

highlights.title: Root address
highlights.text: Use yourbrand.com or go.yourbrand.com with no path after the hostname.

highlights.title: One attached resource
highlights.text: Choose a Link or Public Profile owned by your account.

highlights.title: Verified connection
highlights.text: DNS ownership verification and HTTPS readiness protect the connection.

sections.heading: Connect your domain
paragraphs: In Custom Domains, enter the hostname and choose its Link or Public Profile. Add the DNS records provided by the setup flow at your DNS provider. Keep unrelated website and email records intact.
bullets: Enter a hostname, not a full URL
Wait for DNS and HTTPS readiness

sections.heading: Root-level attachment
paragraphs: A hostname serves one attached resource at its root. It does not create a namespace for all your Links at different /slug paths. The resource's Linktery primary and alias addresses remain separate.
bullets: Edit the resource without rebuilding the connection

sections.heading: Limits and status
paragraphs: Creator Pro includes up to 2 connected custom domains at once; Agency includes up to 10. Free does not include custom domains. Creation and provisioning also have safety limits, so repeated deletion and recreation is not unlimited.
bullets: Share only after the connection is ready

faqs.question: Does a custom domain need a /slug?
faqs.answer: No. It opens its attached Link or Public Profile directly at the root, such as https://yourbrand.com.

faqs.question: Can one hostname open several resources?
faqs.answer: Not as separate /slug paths. Connect a different hostname for another resource, within your plan limit.

faqs.question: Why is my domain still pending?
faqs.answer: DNS propagation and HTTPS setup can take time. Check the records and status shown in Custom Domains before sharing the address.

title: Link rotator
seoTitle: Link Rotator & A/B URL Splitter | Linktery
seoDescription: Randomly split visits between a Link destination and alternative URLs with equal selection chances. Keep one public address for A/B experiments.
lead: Use A/B Traffic Splitter to randomly send visits to your Link destination or one of its alternative URLs.

highlights.title: Equal-chance selection
highlights.text: Each configured destination has the same chance on every visit.

highlights.title: Stable shared URL
highlights.text: Edit alternatives without replacing your campaign's short address.

highlights.title: Campaign experiments
highlights.text: Compare downstream results using consistent UTM values and destination analytics.

sections.heading: Configure the splitter
paragraphs: On Agency, enable A/B Traffic Splitter in the Link editor and add alternative URLs. The resolved main destination is included. Two options give each a 50% chance; custom weights such as 70/30 are not available.

sections.heading: Routing order matters
paragraphs: Device and country rules resolve the main destination before the split. A/B selection then chooses between that URL and the alternatives. An alternative can therefore be chosen after a country match.
bullets: Country rules can override device rules

sections.heading: Evaluate the result
paragraphs: Equal probability does not guarantee equal totals in a small sample, and repeat visitors may reach another option. Click volume alone is not a conversion result; measure sales or signups at each destination.
bullets: Keep all alternatives suitable for your audience
Do not mix unrestricted alternatives with mandatory country routing

faqs.question: Can I set custom weights?
faqs.answer: No. The current splitter selects randomly with equal probability across the main destination and alternatives.

faqs.question: Does it alternate every click?
faqs.answer: No. Each visit is a random selection, so exact totals may differ.

faqs.question: Will country routing always win?
faqs.answer: No. A country rule resolves the main option first, then the split can select that option or an alternative.

title: Geo targeting
seoTitle: Geo-Targeted Links & Country Redirects | Linktery
seoDescription: Route clicks to country-specific destinations while preserving a default URL and recording geographic link analytics in Linktery.
lead: Set country-specific destinations and country-tier rules, with a fallback for other visitors.

highlights.title: Country rules
highlights.text: Map countries to regional stores, language pages, or available offers.

highlights.title: Country tiers
highlights.text: Configure grouped destinations using the tiers available in the editor.

highlights.title: Fallback path
highlights.text: Unmatched geography keeps the previously resolved device or default destination.

sections.heading: Set regional destinations
paragraphs: Start with a default URL, then add country and tier destinations. A specific country match takes priority over a matching tier. Location is an approximate country-level network signal.

sections.heading: Understand rule priority
paragraphs: The redirect starts with the default URL, applies a matching device rule, then applies a country or tier match. No geo match preserves the device-selected URL or default. A/B splitting runs afterward if enabled.

sections.heading: Test your configuration
paragraphs: Check regional availability and always keep a useful fallback. VPNs, carriers, and network data can affect country detection; it is not precise address or identity tracking.

For example, send a matched country to its regional store and keep a general store locator as the default. Confirm that each destination supports the intended currency, shipping region, and language before sharing.

faqs.question: What happens if no country matches?
faqs.answer: The device-selected destination remains, or the default if no device rule matched. An enabled A/B split may still choose an alternative afterward.

faqs.question: Can I target an exact city?
faqs.answer: The current feature provides country and country-tier rules, not exact city or street-address targeting.

faqs.question: Which plans include geo targeting?
faqs.answer: Creator Pro and Agency.

title: Device targeting
seoTitle: Device-Targeted Links for Mobile & Desktop | Linktery
seoDescription: Send mobile, tablet, and desktop visitors to configured destinations while keeping one Linktery short URL and default fallback.
lead: Set separate URLs for mobile, desktop, and tablet visitors from one Smart Link.

highlights.title: Three device types
highlights.text: Configure Mobile, Desktop, and Tablet destinations.

highlights.title: Default fallback
highlights.text: An absent device match keeps the default destination.

highlights.title: Included on Free
highlights.text: Device targeting is available on all current plans.

sections.heading: Configure destinations
paragraphs: Create a Link with a default URL and add the device destinations you need. An unconfigured class uses the default, unless another enabled routing rule changes it.

sections.heading: Know the classification
paragraphs: Device classes come from browser user-agent information, which can be incomplete or unusual. The editor offers broad device classes, not separate iOS and Android rules.

A mobile destination can be a shorter signup page while desktop visitors reach a more detailed product page. Keep both responsive: device classification describes the request and does not guarantee screen dimensions, installed apps, or visitor intent.

sections.heading: Check combined routing
paragraphs: A matching country or tier rule runs after device targeting and can replace its destination. A/B splitting can then choose an alternative. Test the complete configuration, not only the device rule.

faqs.question: Is device targeting included on Free?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is available on Free, Creator Pro, and Agency.

faqs.question: Can I route iOS and Android separately?
faqs.answer: The current editor supports Mobile, Desktop, and Tablet, not separate operating-system rules.

faqs.question: Why did a mobile visitor reach a country page?
faqs.answer: Country and tier rules run after device rules and can override their destination.

title: Link-in-Bio Templates for Every Profile Style
seoTitle: Link-in-Bio Templates for Creators & Brands | Linktery
seoDescription: Explore responsive Linktery public-profile templates, including cinematic covers, compact avatars, banners, portraits, and editorial layouts.
lead: Choose a visual structure first, then customize its card style, avatar, text, and destinations in the profile editor.

highlights.title: Six structures
highlights.text: Switch between cinematic, compact, banner, portrait, editorial, and full-canvas profile layouts.

highlights.title: Responsive by design
highlights.text: Templates adapt their image treatment, spacing, typography, and card layout across phones and larger screens.

highlights.title: Content stays yours
highlights.text: Changing a template changes presentation, not the saved profile name, bio, links, or analytics history.

sections.heading: Choose structure before decoration
paragraphs: A template controls the hierarchy of the profile: where the avatar appears, how much space the hero image receives, and how quickly visitors reach the first destination card.
Linktery keeps the page atmosphere automatic: a soft Sunset blur appears by default, and an uploaded avatar can become the blurred ambient backdrop.

sections.heading: Match the template to the job
paragraphs: Compact Circle prioritizes immediate access to links. Hero Portrait and Classic Cover devote more space to personal branding. Banner Circle supports a familiar social-profile structure, while Cutout Editorial creates a more expressive portfolio presentation.
The best template is the one that makes the profile's primary action obvious on the devices your audience actually uses.

sections.heading: Test with real content
paragraphs: A template can look balanced with three short sample links and still feel crowded with real campaign titles. Preview the actual avatar, bio, cards, and images before publishing.
Check the first screen on a phone, then review tablet and desktop layouts. Long titles and low-contrast backgrounds deserve special attention.
bullets: Use the real avatar and bio

faqs.question: Does changing a profile template delete links?
faqs.answer: No. The template changes the visual structure while keeping the profile content and destinations.

faqs.question: Are Linktery templates responsive?
faqs.answer: Yes. The five profile structures use responsive layouts for phone and larger screens.

faqs.question: Can I also change card colors and styles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Profile Template, Card Theme, Link Card Style, and Social Links Style are available in the editor.

title: Classic Cover Link-in-Bio Template
seoTitle: Classic Cover Link-in-Bio Template | Linktery
seoDescription: Use a cinematic cover image with a soft transition into profile details and responsive link cards in the Linktery Classic Cover template.
lead: A large visual introduction for creators and brands that want the profile image to establish identity before the destination list.

highlights.title: Large cover
highlights.text: Uses a prominent portrait or campaign image at the top of the page.

highlights.title: Soft transition
highlights.text: Blends the image into profile information and link cards.

highlights.title: Brand-first
highlights.text: Works well when visual identity is as important as immediate link density.

sections.heading: Best for visual introductions
paragraphs: Classic Cover gives the opening screen to a cinematic portrait or campaign image. It suits creators, performers, photographers, and personal brands with a recognizable visual identity.
Keep the main subject centered and avoid placing essential details near the crop boundaries.

sections.heading: Prepare the image
paragraphs: Use a high-quality vertical image with enough negative space for responsive cropping. Preview on narrow and wide screens because the visible area changes with the device.
Choose text and card colors that remain readable as the cover fades into the content background.

sections.heading: Keep the action visible
paragraphs: A large cover creates impact but also delays the first link. Put the most important destination first and use a concise bio so visitors can reach it without unnecessary scrolling.
If immediate link access matters more than imagery, compare this layout with Compact Circle.

faqs.question: What image works best for Classic Cover?
faqs.answer: Use a high-quality portrait or campaign image with the subject away from crop-sensitive edges.

faqs.question: Is Classic Cover mobile responsive?
faqs.answer: Yes. The cover and content layout adapt to phone and larger viewport sizes.

faqs.question: Can I change card colors separately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Card Theme is configured separately from the profile template.

title: Compact Circle Link-in-Bio Template
seoTitle: Compact Circle Bio-Link Template | Linktery
seoDescription: Place a small circular avatar above profile details so visitors reach your most important Linktery cards quickly on mobile and desktop.
lead: A focused profile layout with a compact avatar and minimal vertical delay before the first destination.

highlights.title: Fast hierarchy
highlights.text: Shows identity, bio, and the first link in a compact sequence.

highlights.title: Circular avatar
highlights.text: Uses a familiar personal-profile treatment without a large hero image.

highlights.title: Link-forward
highlights.text: Fits creators, consultants, and campaigns where destinations matter most.

sections.heading: Designed for quick choices
paragraphs: Compact Circle keeps the identity block small so more destination cards appear near the first screen. It is a strong default for audiences arriving with clear intent.
The layout works especially well with a concise bio and three to six prioritized links.

sections.heading: Use a recognizable avatar
paragraphs: Because the avatar is smaller, use a close crop, simple logo, or high-contrast portrait. Fine background detail will be difficult to recognize at this size.
Linktery automatically uses a soft Sunset atmosphere or a blurred version of your avatar behind the profile, so the foreground remains the focus.

sections.heading: Prioritize the card list
paragraphs: The compact header gives link ordering more influence. Put the highest-value action first and group related destinations with clear titles.
Avoid repeating the same call to action across several cards unless each destination is genuinely different.

faqs.question: Which template shows links fastest?
faqs.answer: Compact Circle is designed to keep the identity header small and bring the first cards into view quickly.

faqs.question: Does Compact Circle use the avatar as a backdrop?
faqs.answer: Yes. When an avatar is available, Linktery uses a blurred version of it as the ambient backdrop; otherwise it uses the Sunset blur.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for business profiles?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially when a simple logo and immediate access to booking, shop, or contact links are more important than a large hero image.

title: Banner Circle Link-in-Bio Template
seoTitle: Banner Circle Public Profile Template | Linktery
seoDescription: Combine a wide profile banner with a floating circular avatar and responsive Linktery cards for creators, teams, and small brands.
lead: A familiar social-profile composition that separates the brand banner from the person or logo represented by the avatar.

highlights.title: Wide banner
highlights.text: Creates space for campaign art, a landscape image, or brand texture.

highlights.title: Floating avatar
highlights.text: Keeps a recognizable portrait or logo connected to the banner.

highlights.title: Flexible identity
highlights.text: Useful for teams, communities, creators, and branded campaigns.

sections.heading: Two-image storytelling
paragraphs: Banner Circle allows the wide image and avatar to serve different roles. The banner can establish a campaign or environment while the avatar identifies the person, team, or brand.
Avoid putting essential text into the banner because responsive cropping may hide it on some devices.

sections.heading: Coordinate the banner and avatar
paragraphs: Choose images with compatible colors and enough contrast around the floating avatar. A busy banner behind a detailed avatar can make both difficult to read.
Use the profile name and bio for essential information rather than embedding that information into either image.

sections.heading: Responsive behavior
paragraphs: The banner becomes proportionally shorter on compact screens while the avatar remains the identity anchor. Link cards then flow in the standard responsive content column.
Preview the banner at phone width and on a desktop before publishing a major campaign.

faqs.question: Can the banner and avatar use different images?
faqs.answer: Yes. The layout is designed around a wide banner and a separate circular profile image.

faqs.question: Should I place text inside the banner?
faqs.answer: Avoid essential banner text because responsive cropping may hide it. Keep important information in the profile name, bio, and cards.

faqs.question: Who is Banner Circle best for?
faqs.answer: It works well for creators, communities, teams, and small brands that have both campaign artwork and a recognizable avatar or logo.

title: Hero Portrait Link-in-Bio Template
seoTitle: Hero Portrait Creator Profile Template | Linktery
seoDescription: Build an immersive creator profile with identity layered over a large portrait and responsive Linktery cards below the hero section.
lead: An immersive portrait-led layout for creators whose face, character, or visual persona is central to the profile.

highlights.title: Immersive portrait
highlights.text: Uses a strong vertical image as the main identity surface.

highlights.title: Layered details
highlights.text: Places profile identity in close visual relationship with the portrait.

highlights.title: Campaign impact
highlights.text: Fits launches, performers, influencers, and character-led brands.

sections.heading: Use the portrait as the story
paragraphs: Hero Portrait treats the image as more than an avatar. It creates an opening scene around the person or character before the profile moves into destination cards.
Choose an image with a clear focal subject and room for the responsive overlay treatment.

sections.heading: Protect readability
paragraphs: Layered text needs predictable contrast. Use a portrait with a quieter region around the identity text and test both the selected background theme and actual bio length.
If the image contains many bright and dark regions, consider a simpler cover or compact template.

sections.heading: Balance impact and action
paragraphs: An immersive hero creates personality but occupies valuable vertical space. Keep the first card valuable and the number of competing actions under control.
Review card analytics after launch to confirm visitors continue from the portrait into the intended destination.

faqs.question: What photo orientation works best?
faqs.answer: A high-quality vertical portrait with the subject inside safe crop margins is the best starting point.

faqs.question: Is Hero Portrait only for individuals?
faqs.answer: It is strongest for person- or character-led profiles, but a campaign with suitable vertical artwork can also use it.

faqs.question: Can I switch to another template later?
faqs.answer: Yes. Switching templates changes the presentation without deleting the profile's links or saved content.

title: Cutout Editorial Link-in-Bio Template
seoTitle: Cutout Editorial Portfolio Template | Linktery
seoDescription: Use an asymmetric portrait, editorial typography, and responsive Linktery cards for a distinctive creator, artist, or portfolio profile.
lead: A magazine-inspired profile structure with asymmetric imagery and a more expressive treatment of identity and destination cards.

highlights.title: Editorial hierarchy
highlights.text: Uses bold type and asymmetric balance instead of a standard centered profile stack.

highlights.title: Cutout portrait
highlights.text: Makes the profile image feel integrated into the composition.

highlights.title: Distinct card style
highlights.text: Adapts smaller cards to the editorial direction while keeping them usable.

sections.heading: Designed for differentiation
paragraphs: Cutout Editorial is the most expressive Linktery profile structure. It is intended for artists, stylists, photographers, designers, and creators who want the profile itself to feel like part of the portfolio.
The layout still uses responsive HTML content, so profile names and destination titles remain readable and selectable.

sections.heading: Prepare a strong subject image
paragraphs: Choose a portrait with a clear silhouette and enough resolution for larger displays. A simple background and strong edge separation help the cutout treatment feel intentional.
Preview the full composition because asymmetry changes how empty space and long names behave across devices.

sections.heading: Use concise copy
paragraphs: Editorial layouts depend on deliberate hierarchy. Keep the profile name, bio, and destination titles concise so typography remains part of the design instead of becoming visual noise.
For dense resource directories or long descriptions, Compact Circle may provide a more efficient reading experience.

faqs.question: Does Cutout Editorial show a Creator Profile label?
faqs.answer: No. The public template focuses on the user's identity and content without that generic label.

faqs.question: Does the layout work on desktop and mobile?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its spacing, portrait treatment, typography, and cards adapt across viewport sizes.

faqs.question: What content is best for this template?
faqs.answer: It is best for concise, visually led creator or portfolio profiles with a strong portrait and a focused set of destinations.

title: Visual Canvas Link-in-Bio Template
seoTitle: Visual Canvas Link-in-Bio Template | Linktery
seoDescription: Use full-page artwork, a floating profile identity, and layered Linktery cards in the responsive Visual Canvas link-in-bio template.
lead: A full-canvas profile layout for creators and brands that want one image to shape the atmosphere of the entire page.

highlights.title: Full-page artwork
highlights.text: Uses one image as the visual environment behind the complete profile.

highlights.title: Floating identity
highlights.text: Keeps the avatar, name, and social links legible above the artwork.

highlights.title: Layered cards
highlights.text: Places destinations on elevated surfaces so content remains usable over photography.

sections.heading: Build one visual world
paragraphs: Visual Canvas treats the background as part of the profile rather than a separate header. It works well for photographers, artists, travel creators, product launches, and brands with strong campaign artwork.
Choose an image with a clear mood but limited fine detail behind the profile name and first destination cards.

sections.heading: Control contrast before publishing
paragraphs: The balanced overlay helps separate text from the image, but the source artwork still matters. Test bright, dark, and highly saturated areas behind every important element.
Keep essential words in the actual profile content. Text embedded inside the background can be cropped, obscured, or unreadable on smaller screens.

sections.heading: Use imagery without hiding the action
paragraphs: A strong canvas should support the destination list, not compete with it. Put the primary link first, keep card labels concise, and avoid stacking several unrelated visual styles.
If the page needs to present many resources with minimum distraction, compare Visual Canvas with Compact Circle.

faqs.question: Can Visual Canvas use my own background image?
faqs.answer: Yes. Visual Canvas supports a full-page background image with an overlay that helps keep profile content readable.

faqs.question: Does the background replace my avatar?
faqs.answer: No. The background creates the page atmosphere while the avatar remains a separate identity element.

faqs.question: Can I switch away from Visual Canvas later?
faqs.answer: Yes. Switching templates changes the presentation while keeping the profile content and destinations.

title: Free UTM Campaign URL Builder
seoTitle: Free UTM Builder for Campaign Tracking | Linktery
seoDescription: Build a campaign URL with validated UTM source, medium, campaign, term, and content parameters. Copy the result without signing up.
lead: Create a consistently tagged campaign URL in your browser, then shorten and measure it in Linktery if you need ongoing link management.

sections.heading: What UTM parameters do
paragraphs: UTM parameters label a destination URL with campaign context that analytics platforms can read. The most common fields are source, medium, and campaign.
Use stable naming rules so the same channel does not fragment into values such as Instagram, instagram, ig, and instagram-social.
bullets: utm_source identifies the platform or partner

sections.heading: A practical naming convention
paragraphs: Use lowercase values, replace spaces with hyphens, and keep a shared campaign-name list for teams. Do not place personal information or secrets into UTM values because they remain visible in the URL.
After generating the URL, open it once and confirm the destination receives every parameter before distributing it.

faqs.question: Which UTM fields are required?
faqs.answer: The tool requires a destination URL, source, medium, and campaign. Term and content are optional.

faqs.question: Does the UTM Builder store my URL?
faqs.answer: The builder runs in the browser and does not need to save the entered campaign URL to generate the result.

faqs.question: Can I shorten the generated campaign URL?
faqs.answer: Yes. Create a Linktery short link using the generated URL as its destination.

title: Free URL QR Code Generator
seoTitle: Free URL QR Code Generator | Linktery
seoDescription: Generate a QR code for any valid URL in your browser, customize its colors, and download an SVG without creating an account.
lead: Create a scannable SVG for a website, Linktery short URL, or public profile. Use a managed short link when the printed destination may change later.

sections.heading: Static QR code or managed destination
paragraphs: A QR code stores the text you put into it. If that text is a final destination URL, changing the destination later requires printing a new code.
If the QR code contains a Linktery short URL, you can update the short link's destination while keeping the printed QR pattern unchanged.
bullets: Managed short URL for editable campaigns

sections.heading: Printing guidance
paragraphs: Use strong contrast, preserve the quiet margin around the code, and avoid making it too small for the expected scanning distance. SVG is useful for print because it scales without becoming pixelated.
Always scan the downloaded file from more than one device before ordering signs, packaging, cards, or labels.
bullets: Dark foreground on a light background

faqs.question: Is the generated QR code dynamic?
faqs.answer: The QR image itself is static. It becomes operationally editable when it points to a managed Linktery short URL whose destination can be updated.

faqs.question: What format can I download?
faqs.answer: This tool generates a scalable SVG file suitable for web and print workflows.

faqs.question: Do I need an account?
faqs.answer: No account is required to create and download the QR code. An account is only needed to manage a Linktery short URL or public profile.

title: What Is Link Management?
seoTitle: What Is Link Management? A Practical Guide | Linktery
seoDescription: Learn how link management combines short URLs, branded domains, destination updates, QR codes, routing, campaign organization, and analytics.
lead: Link management is the operational layer between the destinations you own and every channel where their URLs are distributed.

highlights.title: Create
highlights.text: Turn destinations into consistent, labeled, shareable campaign links.

highlights.title: Control
highlights.text: Update destinations and rules after a URL or QR code has been distributed.

highlights.title: Measure
highlights.text: Connect clicks, scans, profiles, sources, devices, and campaigns to useful reporting.

sections.heading: From shortening to management
paragraphs: Traditional URL shortening solves a formatting problem: long addresses are difficult to share. Link management solves a lifecycle problem: URLs continue to be used across campaigns after they are created.
That lifecycle includes naming, branding, editing, routing, deactivation, QR distribution, analytics, and access control.

sections.heading: Why campaigns need a link layer
paragraphs: A destination can move, an offer can expire, or a campaign can expand to new regions. Without a managed layer, every published placement has to be found and replaced manually.
A stable public link separates distribution from destination maintenance. Teams can update the managed record while social posts, printed QR codes, and partner placements remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Building a link-management workflow
paragraphs: Start with naming conventions for links and UTM parameters. Assign a destination owner, define how long analytics should be reviewed, and document when a link should be archived.
Use advanced routing only when it serves a clear audience need, and always retain a working default destination.

faqs.question: Is link management the same as URL shortening?
faqs.answer: No. URL shortening is one capability; link management also includes branding, editing, routing, organization, QR distribution, and analytics.

faqs.question: Who needs link management?
faqs.answer: Creators, marketers, affiliates, agencies, and businesses that distribute URLs across multiple channels can benefit from it.

faqs.question: Can public profiles be part of link management?
faqs.answer: Yes. A public profile is a managed landing experience that organizes multiple destination links under one slug.

title: URL Shortener vs Link-in-Bio Page
seoTitle: URL Shortener vs Link-in-Bio: When to Use Each | Linktery
seoDescription: Compare short URLs and link-in-bio pages, understand single- versus multi-destination intent, and choose the right Linktery format.
lead: Both formats use a simple public link, but they solve different visitor decisions.

highlights.title: Short URL
highlights.text: Best when the visitor should reach one destination with minimal interruption.

highlights.title: Public profile
highlights.text: Best when the visitor needs to choose among several destinations.

highlights.title: Shared slug model
highlights.text: Linktery serves both formats from the same domain-and-slug experience.

sections.heading: Choose based on destination count
paragraphs: A short URL is appropriate when there is one intended next step: open a product, join a channel, view a booking page, or visit a campaign landing page.
A link-in-bio profile is appropriate when the visitor may want several actions such as shop, newsletter, portfolio, booking, and social profiles.
bullets: Editable campaign target: managed short URL

sections.heading: Compare the visitor experience
paragraphs: Short URLs reduce the number of decisions but provide less context before the final destination. Public profiles add a branded intermediate page that can explain and prioritize several options.
Every extra choice can reduce focus, so public profiles should still have a clear primary action.

sections.heading: How Linktery resolves /slug
paragraphs: Linktery uses the same public format for both: linktery.com/slug. The slug is checked against active short links and public profiles, and uniqueness rules prevent ambiguous ownership.
This keeps public addresses easy to remember without exposing separate technical path structures to the audience.
bullets: Short link takes its configured redirect flow
Profile renders its configured visual template

faqs.question: Can a Linktery public profile redirect automatically?
faqs.answer: A public profile is intended to present its configured cards. Use a short link when the intended behavior is a single automatic redirect.

faqs.question: Which format is better for Instagram bio?
faqs.answer: Use a public profile when you need multiple destinations. Use a short URL when one campaign destination is the only intended action.

faqs.question: Can the same slug represent both?
faqs.answer: No. A slug must be unique so it resolves deterministically to one public resource.

title: What Is a Smart Link?
seoTitle: What Is a Smart Link? Routing & Analytics Guide | Linktery
seoDescription: Understand how smart links combine a stable URL with device, country, schedule, rotation, fallback, and analytics rules.
lead: A smart link is a managed URL that can select from configured destinations using clear technical rules.

highlights.title: Stable address
highlights.text: The URL shared with the audience remains consistent while rules are managed behind it.

highlights.title: Explicit routing
highlights.text: Device, country, scheduling, and weight rules choose from approved destinations.

highlights.title: Fallback first
highlights.text: A reliable default destination protects visitors when no rule matches.

sections.heading: Smart link components
paragraphs: Every smart link begins with a public URL and a default destination. Optional rules then refine the destination for supported scenarios.
Good configurations are understandable to the link owner and predictable for the visitor. More rules are not automatically better.

sections.heading: Common routing signals
paragraphs: Device classification can separate mobile and desktop journeys. Approximate country signals can select localized resources. Scheduling can activate or expire a campaign, and weighted rotation can distribute an experiment.
Signals have limitations, so each setup needs a working fallback and representative testing.

sections.heading: Smart links and native apps
paragraphs: A smart link can point to a destination format that supports native-app opening, but the handoff depends on the target platform, operating system, installed application, and browser behavior.
Use an accessible web fallback and avoid promising that every environment will open the native app automatically.

faqs.question: Does a smart link always open an app?
faqs.answer: No. App handoff depends on the target platform and visitor environment. Smart links should include a useful fallback.

faqs.question: Can one smart link use several routing rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, but rule priority should be documented and tested so the selected destination remains predictable.

faqs.question: What happens if no rule matches?
faqs.answer: The configured default destination is used.

title: How to Track Link Clicks Across Campaigns
seoTitle: How to Track Link Clicks and Campaign Traffic | Linktery
seoDescription: Learn how to track URL clicks with consistent short links, UTM parameters, referrer data, device context, and campaign reporting.
lead: Reliable click tracking starts before the link is published: define the campaign question, naming convention, and destination first.

highlights.title: Label the campaign
highlights.text: Use consistent names and UTM values before sharing the link.

highlights.title: Track the redirect
highlights.text: Measure visits at the managed link layer across channels.

highlights.title: Connect outcomes
highlights.text: Use destination analytics to compare clicks with signups, sales, or other conversions.

sections.heading: Start with a measurement question
paragraphs: Decide whether you need to compare channels, creatives, partners, destinations, or devices. The question determines how many link variants and UTM values are necessary.
Avoid creating a different URL for every minor placement when the reporting will never be used.
bullets: Which country or device needs a different journey?

sections.heading: Create consistent tracked links
paragraphs: Use one managed short link per meaningful campaign variant and apply a shared UTM convention. Keep source, medium, campaign, and content values consistent across the team.
Test every URL before launch, including query parameters and redirects, because one malformed character can fragment attribution.

sections.heading: Interpret clicks correctly
paragraphs: A click is not automatically a unique person or a conversion. Preview bots, repeated visits, privacy tools, and network conditions can affect traffic counts.
Use click analytics to understand distribution and trends, then combine it with destination-side conversion data for business decisions.
bullets: Review trends instead of isolated spikes

faqs.question: Is a click the same as a unique visitor?
faqs.answer: No. One visitor can click multiple times, and automated clients may also request a link.

faqs.question: Do I need UTM parameters if the link platform has analytics?
faqs.answer: UTM parameters remain useful because they pass campaign context to the destination's analytics system.

faqs.question: Can I track public-profile cards separately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Linktery records profile engagement and card clicks separately from standalone short-link traffic.

title: How to Create a Branded Short URL
seoTitle: How to Create a Branded Short URL | Linktery
seoDescription: Plan a short-link domain, connect DNS safely, choose readable slugs, verify HTTPS, and test branded campaign URLs before launch.
lead: A branded short URL combines a domain your audience recognizes with a concise back-half that explains the destination or campaign.

highlights.title: Choose the host
highlights.text: Use a dedicated root domain or subdomain that is short and clearly associated with the brand.

highlights.title: Connect DNS
highlights.text: Add only the required record and preserve existing website and email configuration.

highlights.title: Name the slug
highlights.text: Use readable, stable back-halves that remain meaningful when a link is shown as text.

sections.heading: Select a domain strategy
paragraphs: A dedicated short domain can be memorable, while a subdomain such as go.example.com is easier to add alongside an existing website. Choose a structure the organization can maintain long term.
Avoid confusing spellings, excessive hyphens, and domains that resemble unrelated brands.

sections.heading: Connect and verify DNS
paragraphs: Review the current DNS zone before adding records. Copy the required record exactly and do not remove MX, verification, or website records that serve other systems.
Wait for verification and HTTPS before publishing the link. DNS propagation time varies by provider and previous TTL settings.

sections.heading: Create and test the short URL
paragraphs: Use a concise slug such as launch, pricing, book, or a campaign name. Avoid dates unless the URL is intentionally temporary.
Test the link on mobile and desktop, confirm query parameters, and verify that the destination remains safe and active.

faqs.question: Can I use my main website domain?
faqs.answer: A dedicated subdomain is usually safer when the root domain already serves a website, because it avoids replacing the existing hosting configuration.

faqs.question: How long does DNS verification take?
faqs.answer: It varies by DNS provider and cached TTL values. Some changes appear quickly, while others take longer to propagate.

faqs.question: What makes a good short-link slug?
faqs.answer: Use a concise, readable term that describes the campaign or action and can remain stable after the destination changes.

title: Dynamic vs Static QR Codes
seoTitle: Dynamic vs Static QR Codes: Key Differences | Linktery
seoDescription: Compare static QR codes with QR codes that point to managed short URLs, including destination updates, analytics, printing, and maintenance.
lead: The visible QR pattern can remain static while the URL encoded inside it points to an editable, managed redirect.

highlights.title: Static destination
highlights.text: The final URL is encoded directly and cannot be changed without replacing the QR image.

highlights.title: Managed destination
highlights.text: The QR code stores a short URL whose redirect target can be updated later.

highlights.title: Analytics layer
highlights.text: A managed URL can record scans as link visits and connect them to campaign reporting.

sections.heading: What a QR code stores
paragraphs: A QR code is a visual encoding of text, commonly a URL. The image does not contact a server or update itself; the camera simply reads the stored value.
A so-called dynamic QR workflow normally encodes a managed redirect URL. The redirect destination changes on the server while the printed QR image stays the same.
bullets: Direct URL encoded in the image
Managed redirect URL encoded in the image
Camera reads the same stored text

sections.heading: When static is enough
paragraphs: Use a direct static URL for permanent resources that are unlikely to move, such as a stable website homepage. It removes a dependency on an intermediate redirect service.
Still test the final QR code and keep control of the encoded domain for as long as the printed material remains in circulation.

sections.heading: When a managed URL helps
paragraphs: Use a managed short URL for packaging, signage, menus, event material, and business cards when the destination may change or scan analytics matter.
Archive and redirect campaigns responsibly because printed codes can continue generating visits long after the original promotion ends.

faqs.question: Can the QR image itself change after printing?
faqs.answer: No. The image remains fixed. A managed redirect changes the destination reached by the URL encoded in that image.

faqs.question: Do dynamic QR codes require internet access?
faqs.answer: A URL-based QR code requires network access to open the encoded URL and follow any redirect.

faqs.question: Can Linktery generate a QR code for a public profile?
faqs.answer: Yes. A public profile URL can be encoded just like a short URL or any other valid HTTPS address.

title: UTM Parameters: A Practical Campaign Guide
seoTitle: UTM Parameters Guide: Source, Medium & Campaign | Linktery
seoDescription: Learn what UTM source, medium, campaign, term, and content mean, how to name them consistently, and how to avoid tracking errors.
lead: UTM parameters pass campaign labels to the destination URL so analytics can group visits by channel, initiative, keyword, and creative.

highlights.title: Source
highlights.text: Identifies where the visitor encountered the link, such as instagram or newsletter-partner.

highlights.title: Medium
highlights.text: Identifies the traffic type, such as social, email, affiliate, or paid-social.

highlights.title: Campaign
highlights.text: Identifies the shared initiative, launch, promotion, or reporting period.

sections.heading: The five common UTM fields
paragraphs: Source, medium, and campaign form the core attribution set. Term is commonly associated with paid keyword context, while content separates creatives, placements, or call-to-action variants.
Only add fields that support a reporting decision. Unused values increase naming inconsistency without improving analysis.

sections.heading: Naming conventions
paragraphs: Analytics systems treat different spellings as different values. Choose lowercase names, a single separator, and a shared vocabulary for channels.
For example, use instagram / social / summer-launch consistently instead of mixing Instagram, ig, SocialMedia, and summer2026 across team members.

sections.heading: UTMs and short links
paragraphs: Build the complete destination URL first, test it, and then use that URL as the managed short-link destination. This keeps the public address clean while preserving attribution at the final page.
If the destination already contains query parameters, append UTM fields correctly using an ampersand rather than a second question mark.

faqs.question: Are UTM parameters case-sensitive?
faqs.answer: Analytics commonly treats differently cased values as separate labels, so a lowercase naming convention is recommended.

faqs.question: Do UTM parameters affect the destination page?
faqs.answer: They are query parameters. Most sites load normally while analytics tools read the campaign labels.

faqs.question: Should UTMs contain customer names or emails?
faqs.answer: No. UTM values are visible in the URL and should not contain personal information or secrets.

title: Public API
seoTitle: Link Management API for Links & Analytics | Linktery
seoDescription: Use the Linktery Public API to manage links, read public profiles, and bring aggregate link analytics into your own tools and dashboards.
lead: Use API v1 to create and update Links, read Public Profiles, and retrieve aggregate analytics for your account.

highlights.title: Link operations
highlights.text: Create and update Links from your application or automation.

highlights.title: Profiles and reporting
highlights.text: Read Public Profile data and aggregate analytics.

highlights.title: Account-scoped access
highlights.text: API keys retain your account's ownership rules and plan limits.

sections.heading: Authenticate server-side
paragraphs: Get an API key from Settings and send it as a Bearer token to the documented API host. Keep it in server-side environment variables, never browser code, public repositories, or exposed logs.
bullets: Key refresh invalidates the old key

sections.heading: Use documented endpoints
paragraphs: API v1 supports Link creation and updates, Public Profile reads, and aggregate analytics. It does not provide unrestricted database access. Check endpoint documentation for accepted fields and pagination.

Start with a read request and inspect the response before adding write operations. Use a separate test Link when validating updates so an integration mistake does not change an active campaign destination.

sections.heading: Handle limits and errors
paragraphs: API access is included on Creator Pro and Agency. Rate and usage limits vary by plan and endpoint, and resource allowances still apply. Use bounded retries for transient errors, not unchanged retries for validation or authentication failures.
bullets: Plan and resource limits remain enforced

faqs.question: Does Free include Public API access?
faqs.answer: No. Public API access is included on Creator Pro and Agency.

faqs.question: Can a key read someone else's resources?
faqs.answer: No. Requests are scoped to the account owning the key and checked against resource ownership.

faqs.question: Can I embed the key in a public website?
faqs.answer: No. Keep it on your server. Refresh a key that has been exposed.

title: Public Profile analytics
seoTitle: Link-in-Bio Analytics & Profile View Tracking | Linktery
seoDescription: Measure Linktery public-profile views, card clicks, engagement trends, countries, devices, browsers, and referrers in one analytics workspace.
lead: Compare visits to your Public Profile with clicks on the individual cards inside it.

highlights.title: Profile visits
highlights.text: Read views and the supported unique-visitor measurements.

highlights.title: Card performance
highlights.text: See which individual destinations receive clicks.

highlights.title: Profile-level scope
highlights.text: Review one profile or the available combined reporting scope.

sections.heading: Views and clicks are different
paragraphs: A view records a profile opening; a card click records a destination selection. One visitor may click several cards, so card clicks can exceed profile views.
bullets: Several clicks per visit are possible

sections.heading: Compare content changes
paragraphs: Review Card Performance after changing titles, images, positions, or offers. Keep the profile and period comparable, and change one important variable at a time.

Record when you publish a change and whether a promotion also changed the incoming audience. A busier card after a campaign launch does not, by itself, demonstrate that its new design caused the increase.

sections.heading: Understand unique counts
paragraphs: Uniqueness is scoped by the reporting logic, including daily and per-profile grouping. Summing days or profiles does not produce a deduplicated count of people. Events can also take a short time to appear.
bullets: Daily uniques are not lifetime uniques
Advanced reports on Pro and Agency

faqs.question: Why can clicks exceed profile views?
faqs.answer: One visitor can open several cards or click again during the same visit.

faqs.question: Can I identify the most-clicked card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Card Performance shows individual card activity for the selected profile and reporting period.

faqs.question: Are combined unique counts distinct people?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Daily and per-profile counts should not be summed as a deduplicated audience across all dates and profiles.

title: Deep linking
seoTitle: Deep Linking for Smart Links with Web Fallbacks | Linktery
seoDescription: Create smart links that attempt supported native-app or external-browser handoffs while preserving a useful HTTPS fallback for every visitor.
lead: Help visitors opening a Link inside a social app continue to the destination in an external browser.

highlights.title: Social app handling
highlights.text: Recognizes supported in-app contexts such as Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.

highlights.title: Best-effort opening
highlights.text: Automatic handoff depends on the source app and device restrictions.

highlights.title: Manual fallback
highlights.text: Visitors can continue manually when automatic opening is blocked.

sections.heading: Enable Deeplink
paragraphs: On Creator Pro or Agency, enable Deeplink in the Link editor and keep a normal HTTP or HTTPS destination. The feature helps with social in-app browsers; it is not an arbitrary native-app URI editor.

sections.heading: The visitor experience
paragraphs: Supported app and device combinations can attempt external-browser opening. Others require an explicit action. Manual opening or copying options remain when the automatic attempt cannot complete.

sections.heading: Test on real devices
paragraphs: Desktop previews cannot reproduce every social-app restriction. Check the source apps and phones your audience uses, and make sure the final page remains usable on mobile.

Open the shared Link from an actual post or message inside the source app. Follow the manual option as well as the automatic attempt, and confirm that visitors can still reach the intended page without repeated prompts.

faqs.question: Will every visit open a browser automatically?
faqs.answer: No. App and operating-system restrictions can prevent it. A manual fallback is provided.

faqs.question: Can I use any native-app URI scheme?
faqs.answer: No. Link destinations must use HTTP or HTTPS. Deeplink is not a general-purpose native-app scheme editor.

faqs.question: Which plans include Deeplink?
faqs.answer: Creator Pro and Agency.

title: How to Create a Link-in-Bio Profile
seoTitle: How to Create a Link-in-Bio Profile | Linktery
seoDescription: Plan, design, publish, and measure a Linktery link-in-bio profile with a clear primary action, useful cards, social links, and mobile testing.
lead: A strong link-in-bio profile is a focused mobile landing page, not a storage place for every URL you have ever shared.

highlights.title: Choose one goal
highlights.text: Decide which action should receive the most attention before adding cards.

highlights.title: Build a clear hierarchy
highlights.text: Use the profile identity, template, card order, and labels to guide the next click.

highlights.title: Measure and refine
highlights.text: Compare profile views and card clicks after making deliberate changes.

sections.heading: Define the profile's primary action
paragraphs: Start with the reason someone opens the page. That may be watching a new release, booking a service, joining a community, shopping a product, or exploring a portfolio.
Place the primary destination early and describe it with an action-oriented card title. Supporting links should help the same audience rather than compete with the main goal.

sections.heading: Choose a template and visual system
paragraphs: Select a template based on the content hierarchy you need. A compact identity area brings cards into view quickly, while portrait and cover layouts give imagery more prominence.
Use readable contrast, consistent card styling, and recognizable icons. Preview the profile at mobile width throughout editing because most bio traffic arrives from a phone.

sections.heading: Publish, test, and measure
paragraphs: Open the public URL outside the editor and test every card, social icon, image, and destination. Check both Wi-Fi and mobile data when the campaign is important.
After publishing, use profile analytics to compare views with managed-card clicks. Avoid redesigning everything after a small number of visits; wait for enough traffic to identify a useful pattern.
bullets: Change one major element at a time

faqs.question: How many links should a link-in-bio profile have?
faqs.answer: Use the smallest set that serves the visitor's likely goals. Prioritize important actions instead of adding links simply because they exist.

faqs.question: Which Linktery template should I choose?
faqs.answer: Choose a compact template when fast access to cards matters most, or an image-led template when the visual identity is central to the page.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the profile works?
faqs.answer: Review profile views, managed-card clicks, and card order over a meaningful period, then test focused changes.

title: How to Read Link-in-Bio Analytics
seoTitle: Link-in-Bio Analytics Guide: Views & Card Clicks | Linktery
seoDescription: Learn how to interpret profile views, daily unique visits, card clicks, clicks per view, locations, devices, and trends for link-in-bio pages.
lead: Link-in-bio analytics are most useful when each metric answers a specific question about reach, page clarity, or destination interest.

highlights.title: Reach
highlights.text: Profile views show how often the public landing page opened during the selected period.

highlights.title: Action
highlights.text: Card clicks show which managed destinations visitors selected after seeing the page.

highlights.title: Context
highlights.text: Country, device, referrer, and time trends help explain changes in traffic.

sections.heading: Start with views and daily unique visits
paragraphs: Total views measure page openings, including repeat visits. Daily unique profile visits reduce repeated activity from the same privacy-preserving visitor signal within a profile and day, but they are not a permanent identity count.
Use both metrics together. A rising gap between total and daily unique visits can indicate repeat interest, repeated campaign exposure, or refresh activity.

sections.heading: Interpret card clicks carefully
paragraphs: Card clicks reveal destination interest, but the highest card may benefit from position as well as copy or relevance. Compare similar periods before and after a deliberate change.
One visitor can select multiple cards during one profile visit. For that reason, clicks per view can exceed 100 percent and should not be presented as a conventional single-action conversion rate.

sections.heading: Use breakdowns to form a hypothesis
paragraphs: A country map can reveal where campaign traffic is concentrated, while device and browser data can expose a mobile-heavy audience. Referrer data can indicate which placements are sending visitors when the source provides a usable referrer.
These dimensions are approximate. Use them to choose a test, then confirm the business outcome in the destination's own signup, sales, or content analytics.

faqs.question: Are daily unique visits the same as unique people?
faqs.answer: No. They are privacy-preserving daily estimates for a profile, not permanent identities across every device and day.

faqs.question: Why can clicks per view exceed 100 percent?
faqs.answer: A visitor can click more than one card during a single profile visit.

faqs.question: Should I optimize using only the most-clicked card?
faqs.answer: No. Consider card position, campaign intent, destination conversions, and enough traffic to make the comparison meaningful.

title: Deep Links and Social In-App Browsers
seoTitle: Deep Links & Social In-App Browsers: Practical Guide | Linktery
seoDescription: Understand how deep links behave inside Instagram and other social webviews, why automatic handoffs can fail, and how to design reliable fallbacks.
lead: Embedded social browsers add another decision-maker between the tap and the destination, so reliable campaigns need more than a custom URL scheme.

highlights.title: Webview constraints
highlights.text: Social applications can block, ignore, or change automatic external navigation behavior.

highlights.title: Destination support
highlights.text: Native-app opening depends on the destination's supported links and the installed application.

highlights.title: Recoverable journey
highlights.text: A useful web page and manual open option protect the visit when automation is unavailable.

sections.heading: Why a link behaves differently inside social apps
paragraphs: Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and other applications can open links in embedded browsers instead of Safari or Chrome. These webviews may handle redirects, cookies, downloads, popups, custom schemes, and user gestures differently.
Behavior can also change between operating-system and social-app versions. A result observed on one phone is not a universal guarantee.

sections.heading: How a safe handoff flow works
paragraphs: First resolve the final approved destination and record the normal redirect context. Then make one best-effort handoff attempt for a supported environment. If the page remains visible, show a concise recovery action instead of starting another automatic cycle.
The fallback should keep the original HTTPS destination available and must never depend on an endless chain between Linktery URLs.

sections.heading: A realistic testing matrix
paragraphs: Test from the actual profile, story, advertisement, or message placement. Cover recent iOS and Android versions, the destination app installed and absent, and the normal system browser.
Track attempted handoffs and fallbacks as operational signals, but do not treat page visibility changes as proof that a conversion occurred.

faqs.question: Why does Instagram sometimes keep a link inside its browser?
faqs.answer: Instagram controls its embedded browser and may restrict external navigation based on platform behavior, operating system, link type, and user interaction.

faqs.question: Can a redirect platform guarantee an external browser?
faqs.answer: No. A platform can attempt supported handoffs, but the source application and operating system make the final decision.

faqs.question: What is the safest fallback?
faqs.answer: Keep a valid HTTPS destination and provide a clear manual open or copy-link action when automatic handoff is unavailable.

title: Create Short Links with the Linktery API
seoTitle: Create Short Links with the Linktery API | Recipe
seoDescription: Create Linktery short links safely from a backend or automation using API authentication, idempotency keys, generated slugs, and predictable errors.
lead: Use this recipe when a CRM, publishing workflow, or internal tool needs to create Linktery links without exposing an API key in the browser.

highlights.title: Server-side authentication
highlights.text: Keep the Linktery API key in a trusted backend or secret store, never in public frontend code.

highlights.title: Safe retries
highlights.text: Send an Idempotency-Key so a network retry cannot silently create a duplicate link.

highlights.title: Owner-scoped result
highlights.text: The API creates and returns a link inside the account that owns the supplied key.

sections.heading: Prepare one authenticated request
paragraphs: Send a POST request to https://api.linktery.com/v1/links from a trusted server. Include Authorization: Bearer followed by the account API key, Content-Type: application/json, and an Idempotency-Key header containing a stable identifier for this creation attempt.

A minimal JSON body needs a valid destination_url. Add a useful title, the supported Linktery domain, and active status when your workflow needs them. Creator Pro receives a server-generated slug; Agency can request an available custom slug.

sections.heading: Treat the response as the source of truth
paragraphs: A successful response includes the Link ID, resolved slug, public short URL, destination, active state, and ETag. Store the Link ID rather than trying to find the record later by its title. Titles are labels and are not unique identifiers.

If the same idempotency key is retried with the same canonical payload, Linktery returns the original resource instead of creating another link. Reusing that key with a different payload returns an idempotency conflict, so generate a new key for a genuinely new link.
bullets: Retain the ETag for future updates
Log the returned request ID for support

sections.heading: Handle failures without unsafe retries
paragraphs: Retry temporary server and rate-limit responses with bounded exponential backoff. Do not retry validation, authentication, plan, or quota errors until the request or account state has changed. Read the rate-limit headers instead of sending an immediate request loop.

When updating the link later, read its current ETag and send it in If-Match with PATCH. This prevents an older automation run from overwriting a newer dashboard edit. API v1 does not expose permanent deletion; set active to false when a link should stop resolving.

faqs.question: Can I call the Linktery API directly from React or browser JavaScript?
faqs.answer: Do not expose a long-lived API key in client code. Call Linktery from your backend, serverless function, or a secured automation environment.

faqs.question: Can every paid plan choose a custom slug through the API?
faqs.answer: No. Creator Pro receives a generated slug, while Agency can request an available custom slug under the current v1 plan rules.

faqs.question: What should I use as the idempotency key?
faqs.answer: Use a stable identifier for one intended creation, such as an internal job or campaign ID. Use a different key for each genuinely new link.

title: Build a Link Analytics Dashboard with the API
seoTitle: Build a Link Analytics Dashboard with the Linktery API
seoDescription: Use Linktery aggregate analytics to build a private dashboard with click totals, time series, locations, referrers, devices, browsers, and operating systems.
lead: Connect Linktery analytics to an internal dashboard without exporting raw visitor events or giving the frontend direct access to a long-lived API key.

highlights.title: Aggregate analytics
highlights.text: Read totals, daily unique click signals, time series, and supported traffic breakdowns for an owned link.

highlights.title: Four reporting windows
highlights.text: Request 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or 90 days using the documented period parameter.

highlights.title: Private integration
highlights.text: Proxy requests through your backend and return only the fields your dashboard needs.

sections.heading: Resolve the links your account owns
paragraphs: Begin with GET https://api.linktery.com/v1/links and store each returned ID with its title and short URL. Use the API's pagination rather than assuming the first response contains every link in a large account.

When a user selects a link in your dashboard, request GET /v1/links/{id}/analytics with period set to 24h, 7d, 30d, or 90d. Linktery checks that the API key owns that link before returning its analytics.
bullets: Never accept an unchecked foreign Link ID

sections.heading: Map the analytics response to useful widgets
paragraphs: The summary contains clicks and server-derived daily unique click signals. The time series is hourly for the 24-hour window and daily for longer periods. Breakdowns contain the leading countries, referrers, devices, browsers, and operating systems available for that link.

Label daily unique clicks accurately: they are privacy-preserving 24-hour visitor signals, not permanent people across all devices and days. The API returns aggregate results rather than raw click rows, which limits personal-data exposure and makes dashboard queries more predictable.

sections.heading: Cache, refresh, and degrade gracefully
paragraphs: Fetch Linktery from your backend, cache a successful response briefly, and let the browser read your own restricted endpoint. A dashboard usually does not need to request every link on every page render. Fetch the selected link first and refresh in response to a user action or a measured interval.

Honor rate-limit headers and use bounded backoff for 429 responses. If analytics are temporarily optimizing, keep the last successful result visible with a clear updated timestamp rather than showing zero. Never log the API key, and refresh it immediately if it may have been exposed.

faqs.question: Can the API return analytics for all links in one request?
faqs.answer: The current v1 analytics route is scoped to one owned Link ID. List the links first, then fetch only the analytics needed by the dashboard.

faqs.question: Does the public API expose raw clicks?
faqs.answer: No. It returns aggregate analytics and supported breakdowns rather than raw visitor-level click records.

faqs.question: Which time zone does the analytics response use?
faqs.answer: The documented v1 response uses UTC and states whether its time-series granularity is hourly or daily.

title: Migrate from Linktree to Linktery
seoTitle: How to Migrate from Linktree to Linktery | Guide
seoDescription: Move a link-in-bio page from Linktree to Linktery with a safe content inventory, analytics archive, profile rebuild, mobile test, and controlled cutover.
lead: Preserve the destinations and records you control, rebuild the public profile deliberately, and change the bio URL only after the Linktery page has passed a real-device check.

highlights.title: Archive first
highlights.text: Save eligible Linktree Insights exports and any audience-contact export before changing the live profile URL.

highlights.title: Rebuild with intent
highlights.text: Use the move to remove stale destinations and establish a clearer mobile card hierarchy.

highlights.title: Controlled cutover
highlights.text: Test the Linktery public URL before replacing the Linktree address across social profiles and campaigns.

sections.heading: Inventory the page before rebuilding it
paragraphs: Record the active card titles, destination URLs, order, social links, profile copy, avatar, and any images you are allowed to reuse. Do not treat screenshots as the only backup; keep a working list where every destination can be opened and checked.

Linktree documents downloadable Insights activity for eligible Premium accounts, including views, clicks, click-through activity, countries, cities, devices, and referrers. Export availability depends on the current Linktree plan. If you collected audience contacts through an integration, export that data separately where the platform permits it.

sections.heading: Build and test the Linktery profile
paragraphs: Create a Linktery Public Profile, choose the template that matches the desired content hierarchy, and recreate only the destinations that still serve a clear visitor goal. Managed Linktery cards can then contribute card-click analytics inside the profile reporting scope.

Open the published URL outside the editor. Test every card and social icon on a phone, verify image crops and contrast, and check the destination after all redirects. Historical Linktree analytics are an archive and are not imported as Linktery profile views or card clicks.

sections.heading: Switch the audience without losing the old record
paragraphs: Replace the Linktree URL in the most important social bio first, then update secondary profiles, pinned posts, email signatures, and campaign assets you control. Keep a checklist so a forgotten placement does not continue sending traffic to an outdated page.

Retain the Linktree page and exported records during a short verification period if your plan and workflow allow it. A Linktree-owned URL cannot simply become a Linktery URL; preserving the exact host and path requires control of the domain and a compatible Linktery configuration.
bullets: Keep an export outside both platforms

faqs.question: Can Linktery import my full Linktree page automatically?
faqs.answer: This guide does not assume an automatic importer. Inventory and rebuild the destinations you control, then verify each one before cutover.

faqs.question: Will my old Linktree analytics appear in Linktery?
faqs.answer: No. Keep the Linktree export as a historical archive; Linktery profile analytics begin when visitors use the Linktery page.

faqs.question: Should I delete the Linktree page immediately?
faqs.answer: A short verification period is safer when available. Confirm important placements and Linktery destinations before retiring the old page.

title: Migrate from Bitly to Linktery
seoTitle: How to Migrate from Bitly to Linktery | Guide
seoDescription: Plan a Bitly-to-Linktery migration using a CSV inventory, staged link recreation, API idempotency, custom-domain checks, and an analytics cutover record.
lead: Treat a short-link migration as an address and data migration: inventory what exists, recreate and verify the new routes, then change traffic in a controlled order.

highlights.title: Export an inventory
highlights.text: Use Bitly's available CSV export to preserve titles, destinations, custom links, engagement totals, and status.

highlights.title: Stage before DNS
highlights.text: Create and test Linktery routes before changing a custom domain or widely distributed campaign address.

highlights.title: Separate analytics eras
highlights.text: Keep historical Bitly engagement data as an archive and mark when Linktery measurement begins.

sections.heading: Classify the links before moving them
paragraphs: Bitly documents an emailed CSV export on eligible paid plans. Its listed fields include the Link, Custom Link, creation date, title, destination URL, engagements, and status. Use that file as an inventory, then remove expired tests and separate high-risk evergreen links from disposable campaign URLs.

Mark links referenced by printed QR codes, paid ads, email automations, mobile apps, or third-party integrations. A QR code continues to open the exact URL encoded in it; creating a different Linktery short URL does not update a printed code.

sections.heading: Recreate links through the dashboard or API
paragraphs: Small inventories can be recreated and checked in the Linktery dashboard. For a controlled batch, use POST /v1/links from a secure backend and give every source row its own stable Idempotency-Key. That makes retries safe if a job stops midway.

Creator Pro receives generated slugs through the API, while Agency can request available custom slugs. Do not assume a Bitly back-half is available until Linktery accepts it. Store the returned Linktery ID and short URL next to the source row so the migration can be audited and resumed.
bullets: One stable idempotency key per row

sections.heading: Cut over domains and reporting carefully
paragraphs: If a custom domain is involved, validate the Linktery configuration and recreate required paths before changing DNS. Lowering TTL in advance can reduce cache duration, but it does not guarantee an instant or zero-downtime change. Keep a rollback record and test from more than one network after the change.

Bitly engagement history is not imported as Linktery click events. Preserve the CSV, record a cutover timestamp, and compare future performance using Linktery analytics from that point. Bitly's own migration guidance also warns that engagement collection begins after links are recreated on the destination platform.

faqs.question: Can I preserve every Bitly URL exactly?
faqs.answer: Only when you control the relevant custom domain, the path is available, and the Linktery plan and domain setup support it. Bitly-owned hosts cannot be transferred.

faqs.question: Will old Bitly clicks appear in Linktery analytics?
faqs.answer: No. Archive the Bitly export and use the migration timestamp as the boundary for Linktery reporting.

faqs.question: What happens to an existing printed QR code?
faqs.answer: It continues to request the URL already encoded in the image. It changes behavior only if that exact host and path remain under your control and are routed accordingly.
